definition: Reproach means to scold; to express disapproval.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word reproach. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know reproach should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: He would gently reproach the borrowers who returned his chisels dull — and then lend them again the next weekend.
A hint leaves the fault unspoken and hopes you find it yourself; a reproach says it aloud, however softly.
Castigate goes far past reproach: the reproached apprentice hears quiet disappointment, while the castigated one is scoured — corrected at length, in heat, and often in public.

To fault someone points out the error, cool and clinical — the inspector faults the wiring and files her report. To reproach carries personal hurt with it: the fault matters because the two of you mattered to each other. Fault keeps its distance; a reproach closes that distance.

To chasten aims to humble and improve — discipline heavy enough to bend someone toward better behavior, the way a crushing loss chastens a boastful team. A reproach is far lighter machinery: one quiet, personal word of disapproval. Chastening reshapes a person; a reproach simply reaches one.

To reproach someone is to hand them their fault wrapped in disappointment — quiet, personal, and heavier than anger.
Reproach is the exact word because the disapproval is spoken, but gently and from close range — between friends, family, people who looked for better from each other.
A rebuke comes down from authority and stings on impact; a reproach rises out of hurt and settles in slowly.
The word does its work in a lowered voice.
Reproach is disapproval at close range and low volume — the word for friends, family, and mentors more than for courtrooms.
Its unit-mate rebuke is the sharp, downward, in-the-moment scolding.
A reproach can even go unspoken, carried in a look; and English lets the noun stand for the state of deserving blame — conduct 'beyond reproach' — a fixed phrase worth recognizing on test day.
